svg.text: Everyday English - Phrasal verbs
trade off
MEANING
To accept less of one desirable outcome in exchange
for more of another.
IN CONTEXT
We are trading off convenience against privacy when
we keep every account signed in.
USAGE NOTE
Trade off X against Y makes the competing priorities
explicit. In American English, trade X for Y is also
natural, but may describe a simple exchange. The
noun is a trade-off, with a hyphen; the verb is trade off.
Specify the cost rather than using trade off as a vague
synonym for decide.
CONVERSATION
A: Could we make the app easier to access?
B: Yes, but we would be trading off security against
convenience.
A: Is there a way to reduce that cost?
B: We could keep a quick login while requiring checks
for sensitive actions.
YOUR TURN
Turn the noun into a verb: There is a trade-off between
speed and accuracy. Model: We are trading off
accuracy against speed. Explain which outcome your
wording prioritizes.
